Checking the settings registry against itself.

Every registered setting declares the kind of value it accepts, as a field, and
carries a default. Nothing asked whether the two agree. A default that its own
field rejects is not a startup error: it surfaces when somebody reads that
setting through the API, which is a long way from the line that caused it.

Defines how large the rsyslog action queue can grow in number of messages stored. This can have an impact on memory utilization. When the queue reaches 75% of this number, the queue will start writing to disk (queue.highWatermark in rsyslog). When it reaches 90% (queue.discardMark), messages start to be discarded, according to LOG_AGGREGATOR_ACTION_QUEUE_DISCARD_SEVERITY. When it is full, every new message, whatever its severity, is dropped if no room frees up within 2 seconds.

Make OIDC users superusers (triggers_superuser, is_superuser) or system auditors (triggers_system_auditor, is_system_auditor) by trigger rule, by a list of exact, case-sensitive usernames, or both. With both, the rule goes first and the list can grant users the rule skips. A user who stops matching loses the flag at their next login, unless remove_superusers or remove_system_auditors is false; an explicit deny by a rule always revokes. A flag with neither is left alone, and an empty list is ignored; to revoke from everyone use the rule {"never": {}}. Username lists are ignored with a warning while Only Superusers Can Set User Emails and Change Usernames (RESTRICT_USER_IDENTITY_TO_SUPERUSERS) is off, since an organization administrator could otherwise rename or create an account to take a listed name. Prefer a rule on a group or the sub claim where that matters.

Messages whose syslog severity number is greater than or equal to this value are discarded while the action queue holds 90% or more of LOG_AGGREGATOR_ACTION_QUEUE_SIZE (queue.discardMark). Severity numbers run from 0 (EMERGENCY) to 7 (DEBUG), so a higher value here discards fewer messages, and 8, the rsyslog default, turns this discarding off. Equivalent to the rsyslogd queue.discardSeverity setting on the action. Job events and activity stream entries are logged at INFO (6), so once LOG_AGGREGATOR_LEVEL lets them through, the default of 5 permits every one of them to be discarded. This setting does not apply once the queue is completely full: each new message, whatever its severity, then waits up to 2 seconds (queue.timeoutEnqueue) for room and is dropped if none frees up. So 8 prevents loss only while the queue has room. Neither kind of discard is logged as an error or a warning.
